what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from the Republic of the Congo in South Africa: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 3352 asylum seekers from the Republic of the Congo in South Africa, 35.5% of all asylum seekers from the Republic of the Congo.
Refugees from the Republic of the Congo, a separate group, live mostly in France, South Africa, the United States and Canada.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Congo from 1997 to 1999 and in 2002 and 2016.
The fact pack does not give other reasons why people left.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 658 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 8800, at the end of 2017; the main years of displacement in the data are 2017 to 2022.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in South Africa.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for South Africa only.
